_meta.baseline: 2026 season for calendar-year leagues (squads as of early 2026)
_meta.continentalNote: Copa Libertadores (47 clubs; 32 in group stage; single-match final at a neutral venue) and Copa Sudamericana. Libertadores 2025: Flamengo (1-0 vs Palmeiras, Lima). Sudamericana 2025: Lanús.

transferWindows.second: Jul - early Sep (verify; calendar shifting from 2026)

leagues.name: Brasileirão Betano (Campeonato Brasileiro Série A)
leagues.continental: Top 4 → Libertadores group stage; 5th-6th → Libertadores qualifying (more if cup winners already qualified); next 6 → Sudamericana; Copa do Brasil winner → Libertadores
leagues.notes: 2025 champions: Flamengo (also won the 2025 Libertadores). Relegated after 2025: Sport, Juventude, Fortaleza, Ceará (verify). Promoted: Coritiba, Athletico Paranaense, Chapecoense, Remo (verify). Mirassol finished in the Libertadores places in their first Série A season.

leagues.name: Série C
leagues.format: Round robin, then two groups of 4 for promotion (top 4 promoted)

countries.stateChampionships: Paulistão (São Paulo), Carioca (Rio), Mineiro, Gaúcho, Baiano, Pernambucano, etc. — Jan-Mar, shortened from 2026. Big local derbies and many smaller clubs that exist mainly for these tournaments.
cups: Copa do Brasil (biggest prize money in the country)
countries.notes: Brazilian clubs sell young talent to Europe at 18 (FIFA rules forbid international transfers under 18, except within the EU/EEA). A teenager breaking through at Palmeiras/Flamengo can be sold for €30m+ (Endrick, Estêvão). Corporate 'SAF' club ownership (Botafogo, Cruzeiro, Vasco, Bahia) is now common.

leagues.name: Liga Profesional de Fútbol (Torneo Betano)
leagues.format: Torneo Apertura (Jan-Jun) and Torneo Clausura (Jul-Dec): two zones of 15, 16 rounds each, then knockout play-offs (top 8 per zone). Relegation by combined annual table and 3-year average ('promedios').
leagues.notes: 2025: Platense won the Apertura (first title in their history); Estudiantes won the Clausura. Relegated end of 2025: Godoy Cruz, San Martín de San Juan (verify). The original prompt listed Colón, Arsenal de Sarandí and Quilmes, who are no longer in the top flight.

leagues.name: Primera Nacional
leagues.format: Two zones; winners promoted, play-offs for more

leagues.name: Primera B Metropolitana / Torneo Federal A
leagues.format: Buenos Aires-area clubs play Primera B Metro; interior clubs play Federal A

countries.notes: The Superclásico (Boca vs River) is the biggest derby in the game. Away fans are banned at most league matches. Economic instability means wages are often paid in USD to keep value.

leagues.name: Liga BetPlay DIMAYOR
leagues.format: 19 rounds, top 8 → two groups of 4 → final
leagues.notes: Relegation by 3-year average. verify 2026 promoted clubs.

leagues.name: Liga de Primera (Mercado Libre)
leagues.notes: 2025 champions: Coquimbo Unido (first title). verify 2026 list.

leagues.name: Liga AUF Uruguaya (Primera División)
leagues.format: Apertura, Intermedio, Clausura, then Championship final
leagues.notes: Rentistas and Sud América (in the original prompt) are in lower divisions.

countries.notes: Uruguay sells young players to Europe very early; a top Nacional/Peñarol youth prospect is a classic story.

leagues.name: LigaPro Serie A (Ecuabet)
leagues.notes: Independiente del Valle's academy is one of the best in the world (Moisés Caicedo, Piero Hincapié, Kendry Páez). Quito's altitude (2,850 m) is an advantage.

leagues.name: Liga 1 (Liga 1 Te Apuesto)
leagues.notes: Universitario won 2023, 2024 and 2025 (verify 2025). Stars: Paolo Guerrero (Alianza Lima).

leagues.name: División Profesional
leagues.notes: Altitude is a core gameplay factor: La Paz (3,640 m), El Alto (4,090 m, Always Ready), Potosí (~3,900 m). Visiting players suffer; acclimatised players gain an edge.
